rules.sentence: Strictly speaking, acute symptomatic seizures cannot be diagnosed as epilepsy, however, acute symptomatic seizure is a common symptom in older adults, which increases the risk of developing epilepsy.
Epilepsy persists in one-third of these patients with acute symptomatic seizures.

A study has shown that acute symptomatic seizures are the most common risk factors of SE and/or cluster seizures in the elderly, which is a neurologic emergency; this phenomenon increases the risk of neurologic emergency for the elderly.
A recent study conducted in the US of adult patients (most of whom could be considered elderly) in several intensive care units, highlights the immune origin of the novo new-onset refractory SE.
In this case, immunomodulatory treatment is more effective than antiepileptic drugs.
